title: Do the last two digits tell us everything about four?
description: Three statements about the last two digits of a number are tested by splitting numbers into hundreds and last two digits. The hundreds are whole fours, so all three statements hold, and Keeko's doubt about numbers that end in two zeros is broken.
teaching_notes: One idea: the hundreds part is always a whole number of fours, so the number and its last two digits are divisible by four together. Watch for students who think a number ending in two zeros is a special case.

source: Consider these statements: 1. Only the last two digits matter when deciding if a given number is divisible by 4. 2. If the number formed by the last two digits is divisible by 4, then the original number is divisible by 4. 3. If the original number is divisible by 4, then the number formed by the last two digits is divisible by 4. Do you agree? Why or why not?
video_script.why: The child sees that the hundreds part is always a whole number of fours, and uses this to test each of the three statements with a number.
video_script.substitution: Split the number into the hundreds part and the last two digits, and compare how many fours each part holds.
video_script.anchor: three statement cards, and numbers split into a hundreds part and the last two digits
video_script.wrong_answer: a number that ends in two zeros cannot be divisible by four
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says a number that ends in two zeros cannot be divisible by four, because the last two digits make zero. Zero fours is a whole number of fours, and one thousand two hundred is three hundred fours, so the bubble is struck through.
video_script.payoff_line: Yes, all three statements are true

final_answer.value: Yes, all three are true. Examples: 124, 364, 4028 are divisible by 4
final_answer.spoken: yes, all three are true, and one hundred and twenty four, three hundred and sixty four and four thousand and twenty eight are divisible by four

hold_back: Answer: Yes, all three are true. Examples: 124, 364, 4028 are divisible by 4
maths_rules: 100 = 25 x 4 and 1000 = 250 x 4, so the hundreds part of any number is a whole number of fours
so the hundreds part never changes the answer, and only the last two digits matter
124 = 100 + 24, with 100 = 25 fours and 24 = 6 fours, so 124 = 31 fours
364 = 300 + 64, with 300 = 75 fours and 64 = 16 fours, so 364 = 91 fours
if the whole and the hundreds part are whole fours, then so is the difference, which is the last two digits
1200 = 12 hundreds = 12 x 25 fours = 300 fours, and 00 = 0 = 0 x 4
video_script.design: One idea: the hundreds part is always whole fours, so the number and its last two digits are divisible together. Assumes the test for four by the last two digits. Wrong idea: two zeros at the end are a special case. The three statement cards stay on the board to the end.

narration: <bookmark mark='ex'/>Step two, test the second statement with one hundred and twenty four. It is one hundred plus twenty four.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>One hundred is twenty five fours, and twenty four is six fours. Together they make thirty one fours.
<bookmark mark='more'/>The same works for three hundred and sixty four. Three hundred is seventy five fours, and sixty four is sixteen fours.

narration: <bookmark mark='ex'/>Step three, test the third statement with four thousand and twenty eight. It is four thousand plus twenty eight.
<bookmark mark='whole'/>The whole number is one thousand and seven fours, and four thousand is one thousand fours.
<bookmark mark='take'/>Take away the thousand fours, and seven fours are left, which is twenty eight. The third statement is true.

marks.check: 124 / 4 = 31 is written and a tick appears
marks.more: 364 / 4 = 91 and 4028 / 4 = 1007 are written and ticks appear

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, check by dividing.
One hundred and twenty four divided by four is thirty one.
<bookmark mark='more'/>Three hundred and sixty four divided by four is ninety one.
Four thousand and twenty eight divided by four is one thousand and seven.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks a number that ends in two zeros cannot be divisible by four.
The reason is that the last two digits make zero.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>But zero fours is a whole number of fours, with nothing left over.
<bookmark mark='twelve'/>Take one thousand two hundred. It is twelve hundreds, which is three hundred fours.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Two zeros at the end fit all three statements.
